statements.statement: Vertical scaling involves adding more machines to a system to enhance performance.
statements.explanation: Vertical scaling focuses on upgrading a single machine's resources, while adding more machines is known as horizontal scaling.

statements.statement: Vertical scaling can be limited by the maximum capacity of a single machine.
statements.explanation: Vertical scaling can only increase a machine's resources up to its maximum capacity, after which no further enhancements can be made.

statements.statement: Vertical scaling requires significant changes to the application architecture.
statements.explanation: One of the benefits of vertical scaling is that it improves performance without necessitating changes to the application architecture.

statements.statement: Upgrading CPU and RAM are examples of vertical scaling.
statements.explanation: Vertical scaling involves increasing a machine's resources, such as its CPU and RAM, to improve its performance.
